name: IMF programme + fiscal crisis
story: Pakistan was negotiating a stalled IMF Extended Fund Facility through early 2022. Federal liquidity was already strained — no spare capacity for pre-emptive monsoon spending.

name: Tarbela + Mangla dams — silted
story: Pakistan's two largest dams have lost ~25–40% of their original storage capacity to sediment build-up by 2022, severely reducing the buffer they provide against monsoon spikes.

name: Karakoram anomaly reversal
story: The Karakoram glaciers were historically advancing (Hewitt 2005 'Karakoram Anomaly'). NASA GRACE-FO mass balance now shows ~6 Gt/yr loss — the anomaly has flipped. The reservoir of frozen water is shrinking.

name: KP + Gilgit-Baltistan deforestation
story: Hansen Global Forest Change v1.11: KP + Gilgit-Baltistan lost ~27% of forest cover from 2000 to 2020. National forest cover ~4.8% — among Asia's lowest. Less canopy = faster runoff to the Indus.

name: 2010 floods reconstruction — never completed
story: Many of the embankments and homes destroyed in the 2010 floods (the previous record event) were never rebuilt to higher resilience standards — the same villages were hit again in 2022.

name: La Niña — third consecutive year
story: Rare triple-dip La Niña caused anomalous easterly winds across the northern Indian subcontinent. Nanditha et al. (2023) link this directly to the 2022 monsoon intensity via a stationary Rossby wave pattern.

name: Political crisis — Imran Khan ousted
story: Vote of no confidence removed PM Khan two months before the monsoon. Cabinet transition and IMF re-negotiations distracted federal government from pre-monsoon disaster preparation.

name: Climate Change Authority — chronically underfunded
story: Federal climate adaptation budget stayed under USD 5 M per year through FY2022 — Pakistan has no FEMA-equivalent disaster reconstruction fund.

name: GLOF cluster across Gilgit + KP
story: At least 16 documented Glacial Lake Outburst Floods across Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa during 2022, pre-saturating Indus tributaries before the monsoon even arrived.

name: Arabian Sea SST anomaly
story: Arabian Sea surface temperatures ran 1.5–2 °C above the 1981–2010 average. Warmer sea = more evaporation = more moisture feeding the southerly monsoon flow into Sindh and Balochistan.

name: March–May 2022 heatwave
story: Pakistan + northwest India recorded the hottest March in 122 years. Jacobabad hit 51 °C in June. Pre-monsoon heat dried out the topsoil (less infiltration) and accelerated upstream glacial melt.

name: Shisper Glacier outburst (GLOF)
story: Glacial Lake Outburst Flood in Hunza destroyed the historic Hassanabad Bridge — three months before the Sindh floods downstream. Same crisis, opposite ends of the country.

name: Early monsoon onset
story: The 2022 monsoon arrived ~2 weeks earlier than the long-term average — overlapping with the tail of the pre-monsoon heatwave and the GLOF discharge surge.

name: Sukkur Barrage — 1930s design limit
story: Designed for a peak discharge of 1.5 M cusecs in the colonial era. Aug 27 2022 peak: 1.8 M cusecs — operators had to release water in uncontrolled bursts.
